changelog: fix: report_builder.py stated the haemoplasma nomenclature backwards in four places. It described Eperythrozoon and Haemobartonella as superseded names transferred into Mycoplasma in 2001. The transfer proposed in 2001 was never validly published and Judicial Opinion 92 (2014) denied the Request to place the new combinations on the Approved Lists, so those two are the names LPSN treats as correct. Merging the two rows was always right — one group should not appear twice — but the reason printed under it was wrong, and it went out in two customer-facing reports. The merged row is now labelled 'Haemoplasma group' instead of 'Mycoplasma (haemotropic)', and the note explains the actual nomenclature. The same note no longer asserts arthropod vectoring: transmission has been documented in a closed dog population on ectoparasiticides and earlier flea evidence attributed to misidentification, so recovery from an ectoparasite sample is not by itself evidence of a vector.
